topic: Cross-lingual Offensive Language Detection: A Systematic Review of Datasets, Transfer Approaches and Challenges
topic_definition: Stage 1 observable projection of the original paper's eligibility. Use title and abstract evidence to judge whether the study concerns cross-lingual or multilingual offensive-language, hate-speech, abusive-language, or toxic-content detection/classification with language-transfer framing.
summary: Stage 1 title/abstract projection of source-faithful Stage 2 criteria; executable publication cutoff is handled by cutoff_jsons/2401.09244.json.

summary_topics.description: Cross-lingual Offensive Language Detection: A Systematic Review of Datasets, Transfer Approaches and Challenges

required.criterion: Title/abstract indicates offensive-language, abusive-language, hate-speech, toxic-content, sexism, racism, misogyny, cyberbullying, or related harmful-language detection or classification.
Title/abstract indicates a cross-lingual, multilingual, zero-shot, few-shot, code-switching, source-target-language, or language-transfer setting.
When offensive-language detection and cross-lingual or multilingual framing are visible but the exact transfer mechanism is incomplete, keep maybe and defer final confirmation to Stage 2.

exclusion_criteria.criterion: Title/abstract clearly indicates transfer only across non-language dimensions such as platforms, domains, datasets, or topics, with no language-transfer component.
Title/abstract clearly indicates low-resource-language work without any knowledge-transfer approach.
Visible metadata or title/abstract clearly indicates a competition report, shared-task system paper, Master's dissertation, or PhD dissertation.
